title: Verse Box
kicker: A FAIR GO IN THE AGE OF SUPERINTELLIGENCE
description: A proposed public introduction to personal intelligence, learning and participation.

blocks.text: Learn, explore and shape your own path with an Aura that belongs to you.

Verse Box is a proposal for a portable public demonstration on Minjerribah, also known as North Stradbroke Island, and in the wider Redlands area in Queensland. A trial would give residents and visitors access to demonstrations, equipment and assistance with personal or community projects.

Aura of Intelligence, or Aura, is proposed as a personal artificial intelligence (AI) environment that belongs to its operator and grows with their experience. Inspired by an aura or halo around a person, it would work across computerised devices, including wearables and smart devices. It is designed to provide a fair go in the age of superintelligence, helping people learn faster, know themselves, think independently and navigate choices across everyday life, work and public participation.

rows: Learn and think
Explore an idea, practise a skill and compare explanations with sources.
Live, travel and work
Plan a journey or business activity, or find the rules, services and legal pathways relevant to a situation.
Know yourself and create
Reflect on experience, recover project memories, make creative work or explore a measured avatar.
Participate in public life
Understand an issue, compare proposals, contribute and follow decisions.

blocks.text: A fair go and Joyful Responsible Abundance

A fair go means access to intelligence, learning and a voice in decisions that affect your life. Joyful Responsible Abundance connects that access with freedom to enjoy life, responsibility for consequences and benefits shared more widely. Reusing suitable second-hand equipment would help keep the trial budget low. [1, pp. 2-7; 4, pp. 8-18]
Hosts, locations, dates, activities, costs and contact arrangements would be agreed before a public invitation.
Prepared by Luke Nathan Hayes, Aura of Intelligence. Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Queensland, Australia.
Choose your own adventure

Begin with an interest, question or project. Your Aura could develop through everyday use, with tools added as your interests grow. You would choose the devices and services you trust, the information you share and the work your AI does on your behalf.

title: A first visit
description: Explore an interest, review the result and continue on your own device.

blocks.text: The proposed public station would combine demonstrations, assisted activities and access to the website or application.
Explore an interest

A host could help someone explore a skill, a project or a local issue. An everyday question might lead into travel planning, a business decision or finding an appropriate legal pathway before seeking advice. Demonstrations would use sample records.
Review the result

A session might produce a sourced explanation, body measurements, a creative work or a draft community proposal. The participant could inspect the inputs, correct errors and save the result to their own device.
Continue on your own device

A QR code or web address would open the website, with an application available for installation. Personal records would be collected and organised on the participant's device or browser storage. Assistance with transfer would be available for people using the public equipment.

rows: Computers and displays
Reuse suitable second-hand equipment, including ex-government or business mini PCs that meet the requirements for operating the sensors and applications.
Sensors, capture and measurement
Cameras, phone mounts, lighting and measuring tools for the activities offered. Check driver support, connections and calibration with the intended computer.
Portable flatpack structure
A transportable station with braced framing, stable feet, secure equipment mounts and clear assembly instructions.

blocks.text: Candidate computers would be checked for software and driver support, connections, memory, storage and performance with the sensors and applications running together. Selection would consider condition, repairability and total cost.

title: An Aura of your own
description: A personal AI environment for memory, learning, creativity and everyday choices.

blocks.text: An Aura would connect its operator's memories, interests, skills, values, relationships, body references, projects and questions. The operator would control the personal archive, access settings and direction of development. Connected AI could search this context, explain connections and assist with ongoing work. [1, pp. 5-6; 3, pp. 4-11]
Aura's boundary is "clothing, not skin": an external, removable system. Its operator would be able to stop using it and delete their personal archive.
Context over time

Returning to a project after several months could bring back its goals, sources, decisions, results and subsequent changes. The operator could follow the reasoning behind an earlier decision and update the record as the work develops.
Learning and digital hygiene

Aura could help its operator learn quickly, compare sources, question assumptions and test explanations. Digital hygiene would include recognising deceptive or manipulative material, reviewing incoming connections and controlling sharing. These tools would support independent judgement when encountering advertising, political messaging, synthetic media or automated accounts.
Digital twins

A digital twin is a computer-based representation linked to a person, place or activity. A personal twin might combine a measured body model with records of experience. A place twin might represent a room, garden or public path. Records identify measured observations, personal accounts, interpretations and simulations.
The spatial interface

Aura's spatial design draws on aura and chakra imagery. Seven nested horn tori organise information around a person and meet at a central infinity point. Personal data occupies the internal faces of the hollow geometry, with additional privacy conditions. Public data occupies the external surfaces. Records receive addresses within this structure and can be explored through spatial views, lists, text or voice. [8; 11]
Sharing
The operator only shares information or content that is useful to the situation and does not cause them a privacy concern.
Choose the experiences that interest you

An Aura could grow across the activities that matter to its operator. Expansion options would describe their functions, equipment, data access, costs and support. [3, pp. 4-11; 1, p. 6; 4, pp. 15-18; 2, pp. 1-3]

title: An Aura that fits your life
description: Choose the devices, services, budget and support that suit you.

blocks.text: An everyday Aura would be planned with the person using it. Their brief would describe the activities, privacy requirements, trusted devices and services, budget and support.

rows: Purpose and interaction
Which personal, work or community activities would you like help with? Text, voice, pictures or spatial views? When is initiative welcome?
Ownership and continuity
Which records, configurations and model adaptations would you own and be able to take with you? What depends on a provider's licence or service?
Privacy priorities
Which information feels private or secret? Which uses feel acceptable? How do convenience, capability, effort and cost weigh against privacy?
Trust and location
Which devices, people, providers and locations do you trust for particular jobs? What evidence would help you decide?
Practical life
What equipment and records exist already? How do travel, household life, access needs and connectivity affect the arrangement?
Support and change
Who maintains things? What help is welcome? How would you pause, simplify, move or end the arrangement?

blocks.text: Example brief

"I want help finding my earlier writing, learning music and following local planning proposals. I prefer my existing phone and a service I trust to process selected writing. I want an export I can use elsewhere and a monthly spending limit."
Compare suitable arrangements

An equipment or service proposal would show where information travels, who can access it, setup and running costs, maintenance and support. The person could compare alternatives against their brief before purchasing equipment or connecting a service. [4, p. 40]
Where would the work happen?

An Aura could use on-device processing, home equipment, online services or a combination. The arrangement would identify where records are stored, where applications process them and how backups are recovered.

rows: Existing device and online services
A phone or computer with connected applications and storage.
Provider access, terms, recurring cost and export formats.
Device-led personal Aura
Local records and supported on-device functions.
Capacity, battery use, backup and available functions.
Home storage; selected processing
An archive at home, with particular jobs run locally or elsewhere.
Remote access, transfer time, administrator access and retained copies.
Home computing and devices
A computer, storage and connected sensors sized for the workload.
Equipment, energy, noise, maintenance, travel access and performance.
Managed or cooperative support
Storage or processing through a service operator or shared facility.
Administrator access, account separation, governance, cost and migration.
Isolated workspace
A local-only network or physically disconnected device and archive.
Imports, updates, exports, recovery and available functions.

blocks.text: Combine the parts that fit

For example, online tools could process project documents while family recordings remain on home storage and a dedicated device holds secret material. A managed service could provide storage, processing and backup under an agreement covering operator access, retention and migration.
Browser-based personal tools would need usable export and recovery because storage quotas and automatic clearing can affect retained records. [T5]

title: Public, private and secret
description: Decide who can access your information, for which purpose and under what conditions.

blocks.text: Public, private and secret views would organise information according to the operator's privacy requirements. Access settings would apply to applications, people and outward releases. [2, pp. 29-31]

rows: Public / outward
An approved biography, qualification, proposal or contribution statement.
Exact wording or media, audience, purpose, date and correction route.
Private
Project history, personal reflections, selected health records or relationship context.
Which functions and people receive access, where processing occurs and for how long.
Secret
An especially intimate account, closely held recollection or other sensitive material.
More closely bounded interpretation, training and disclosure; separate protection where chosen.

blocks.text: Permissions
Permissions would name the material, use, recipient or process, location and duration. Storage, interpretation, model training, external actions and publication would have their own access settings.
Derived records and models

Transcripts, summaries, search representations and trained models may retain information from their sources. They would inherit the source restrictions. Public-facing applications would receive approved outward records through controlled access.
Keys and access

Accounts, encryption keys, separate stores and application controls would implement access restrictions. The agreement would identify key holders, applications with readable access, and support or household accounts. [T1]
Operator control

The design gives governments and technology companies no built-in access to personal archives. Release to a public archive or research trial would be a separate, informed action by the operator, under stated conditions.

The operator would be able to delete their personal archive, backups and derived personal models. Public and research releases would separately state how already shared material is retained, withdrawn or deleted.
Who gets access, and for what?

A provider might hold encrypted backups while another service processes selected records. The personal plan would identify the information each service receives, who can read it and what copies it retains.

rows: Working storage
The main records and copies, their locations, protection, availability and authority when versions differ.
Interpretation and search
Which records go to the chosen processor, in what form, for which job and with what access.
Personal model training
The selected dataset, model, processing location, retained inputs, outputs and provider reuse terms.
Backup and recovery
Where copies live, who holds keys, who helps after loss and how a restore is demonstrated.
Support and maintenance
Who administers the equipment or account; what support access exists while it is unlocked.
Chosen disclosure
The named recipient, selected representation, purpose, retention and correction or withdrawal route.

blocks.text: Encryption and processing access

Encryption protects information in transit and in storage. Processing may require readable information, so the plan would also identify the processing environment, administrator access and retained logs or copies.
Checking an arrangement
Checks would include service terms, software inspection where available, a demonstration of data transfers and permissions, an export in a usable format and recovery from a backup.
Revoking permission would block pending transfers and future access. For delivered copies, the release record would identify the recipient's retention, correction and deletion process. [2, pp. 27-31]
When stronger separation is wanted

Stronger privacy arrangements would be designed around the information to protect, the likely sources of access and the person's maintenance preferences. Options include app permissions, dedicated devices, local networks and physically disconnected workspaces.

rows: App permissions
Limits access to files, sensors and connected accounts.
Permission coverage, provider telemetry and onward processing.
Dedicated device or profile
Separates accounts, app data and device use.
Operating-system support, administrators, backups and recovery.
No active SIM/eSIM; home Wi-Fi
Removes the ordinary mobile-data connection.
Internet-enabled Wi-Fi still permits uploads.
Local-only home network
Connects approved local devices while blocking internet routes for that network.
Other connections, local relays, name lookups and what happens on reconnection.
Physically disconnected workspace
Separates the device from online and household-network services during secret work.
Controlled imports, updates, backups, physical access and reviewed exports.

blocks.text: Local network configuration

A local-only network would block outgoing internet routes for both IPv4 and IPv6, the two common internet addressing systems. Configuration would also cover permitted local services, devices that can forward information and automatic synchronisation. [T1; T7]
Phone options

Apple documents app sandboxing, which separates apps' private files, and a local-network permission distinct from internet access. On compatible hardware, GrapheneOS offers user profiles and a per-app Network permission covering local networks too. [T2-T4]
Apps may queue uploads for reconnection. An offline setup would include a checked import, update and reconnection process. [T6]

title: Records, sensors and twins
description: Connect chosen records, measurements and sensors with a digital representation.

blocks.text: Inputs could include documents, photographs, recordings, body measurements, wearables and environmental sensors. The capture plan would specify sources, recording conditions, storage and processing.

rows: Notes and files
Memory, learning, projects and references.
Selected folders or records, dates, source rights, other people's information and corrections.
Voice and video
Conversation context, creative practice or reflection.
Initiation or standing permission, visible recording state, shared spaces, retention and processing location.
Measurements and images
Body modelling, avatars and simulation.
Measured and inferred details, capture conditions, accuracy and audience.
Biosensors (optional)
Map body signals and connect them with personal context and the digital twin.
Sensor choice and number, recording rates, calibration, vendor access and permitted uses.
Home and environment
Resources, comfort, gardens and automation.
Rooms, devices, household boundaries, permitted actions and manual control.
Earlier archives
Connect earlier records with current work.
Size, ownership, dates, duplicates, retention and import formats.

blocks.text: Recording conditions that fit daily life

Capture could be started for each activity or follow a recurring schedule. Standing permission would specify the device, place, duration and uses, with controls to pause or change recording. Shared-space capture would require agreement with the people involved.
Keep sources and interpretations distinct

A person's words, a measured signal and an AI interpretation have different meanings. A record retains the source, time, conditions and uncertainty where relevant. A correction adds the changed understanding and updates the dependent working records. [2, pp. 25-31]
Represent the parts of life that matter
Body and place models could support avatars, measurements, inventories, maintenance and planning. The required accuracy and detail would depend on the application.
A measured body reference

Capture would use measured height, a defined arm-span pose and shoulder-width measurements as reference points. Repeated readings would help assess measurement error. Front and side images would use consistent framing and lighting. The record would retain original images, measured dimensions and software estimates.

An avatar is a digital representation of a body or character. Its proportions could come from measurements, photographs or reconstruction software. Each model would record its sources, method and measured accuracy. [9, slides 8-10]
A home or place reference

A room, garden or workshop model might hold inventories, maintenance notes, photographs, resource observations or different layout ideas. A simulated change is labelled as a possibility and compared with actual observations after an agreed action. [6, pp. 9-11]

rows: Find a possession or maintenance record
Selected locations and records, with separate access for each person.
Understand resources or comfort
Chosen observations or sensors, their operators and the information retained.
Operate a selected device
The particular action, resources involved, review conditions and manual control.
Plan a change together
An agreed shared view, assumptions, affected people and the later outcome.

title: Aura Genesis
description: An optional programme for an ultra-high-definition Aura twin and twin socialising.

blocks.text: Genesis is a proposed, separate opt-in programme for developing an ultra-high-definition Aura twin and learning to work with it through twin socialising. It is not required for Verse Box, an everyday Aura, C-Hours or civic participation. [2, pp. 1, 15]
Biosensors chosen by the participant

Participants choose which compatible biosensors to use and how many. These map the quantified self: measured biological signals that help the twin reflect its operator's biology. The sensors are external and removable.

Options include scalp EEG for brain electrical activity, ECG or optical pulse, breathing sensors, oxygen saturation, blood pressure, skin conductance, temperature, eye tracking, movement and surface EMG for muscle activity. The full chosen suite would be visible in the participation agreement. [2, pp. 17-18]
Sessions and twin socialising

The proposed pressure programme is 60 two-hour sessions, totalling 120 hours. Cameras, microphones and all installed biosensors would record throughout each defined session, including rest. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) uses oxygen in a pressurised chamber; clinical assessment, equipment and operating conditions would have a participant-specific plan. [2, pp. 1-3; T8]

Afterwards, twin socialising would practise memory, timing, initiative, correction and approved tool use in everyday life. Recording outside pressure sessions would have its own start and stop permissions. [2, pp. 15, 34]
Research and outward release

Truth Engine research would examine patterns around truthful answers, instructed falsehoods, uncertainty and changed understanding. Its methods and results would require evaluation. Research participation and release of personal data would each have their own agreement.

A public or research release would identify the exact information, recipient, purpose, retention and withdrawal conditions before the operator commits it. The personal archive would remain under the operator's control, with removal and deletion choices. [2, pp. 29-31]
Plan for the record you create

Genesis storage would include the complete chosen biosensor suite, cameras and microphones throughout pressure sessions, alongside existing records, models and backups. The number of sensors, recording rates, duration and retention determine the capacity required. [2, pp. 25-28]
The proposed Genesis application would be developed and validated to Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) standards, with controlled acquisition, secure storage and tested recovery. [T9]
Illustrative video storage across 120 hours

Bitrate is the amount of data recorded each second. These estimates use the combined average video bitrate of all cameras and decimal terabytes, or TB. Add capacity for audio, sensors, models, other files and growth.

25 megabits/second

100 megabits/second

blocks.text: Calculation: TB = megabits/second x hours x 3,600 / 8,000,000.

rows: Biosensor archive
Every chosen stream at its configured channel count, recording rate and precision, with timestamps, calibration and quality records.
Media and earlier records
Camera and microphone recordings, imported history and source references.
Working records
Transcripts, search indices, selected clips and display copies.
Models and processing
Base models, adapted versions, temporary working files and computer memory.
Recovery and growth
Backup versions, retention, expected new capture and reserved capacity.

blocks.text: Measure a representative sample
Record a representative sample with the selected equipment. Measure each camera, microphone and biosensor stream, then project the complete programme, backups, model work and growth.

title: Developing a personal AI
description: Build context, use and correct responses, and evaluate personal model adaptation.

blocks.text: A language model is trained software that works with language. Large language model is commonly shortened to LLM. Aura's proposed nanoLLM would be a compact personal model adapted to its operator's tasks, preferences and available computing.
Build the personal dataset

The dataset would bring together source records, context, examples of desired responses and the operator's corrections. Everyday use would reveal missing information and recurring errors. Reviewing those cases would develop the material for personalisation and possible training.

rows: Define the task
Describe the intended result, representative situations and criteria for a satisfactory response.
Prepare sources
Link records to their dates, origins and access conditions; retain the operator's context and corrections.
Use and correct
Review responses, record errors and add examples of the operator's preferred response.
Review coverage
Check missing context, contradictions and variation across situations.
Consider training
If retrieval is insufficient, assess adaptation methods, training examples, computing needs, cost and access settings.
Evaluate
Test on examples withheld from training and compare performance with the current arrangement, including uncertainty and privacy behaviour.

blocks.text: Retrieval and training

Retrieval supplies relevant records to a model when it handles a task. Training changes the model using approved examples. Retrieval could provide personal context before adaptation is needed. Models trained on private or secret sources would inherit their access restrictions. [2, pp. 27-31]
The model record would include its task, training sources, processing location, evaluation results and known limits.

title: A fair go in the age of superintelligence
description: Wider access to intelligence, ownership, useful capability and a voice in decisions.

blocks.text: Superintelligence describes a possible level of AI capability exceeding human performance across many kinds of task. The fair-go question asks how growing capability could expand people's practical choices, understanding and share in the result. [1, pp. 2-7]

The United States and China are competing to lead increasingly powerful AI. This work proceeds on the view that Australians need practical ways to shape and benefit from the transition towards possible superintelligence. Aura, C-Hours and P4A are being developed to strengthen everyday people's understanding, participation, ownership and share in the benefits. The UNGA81 contribution frames this work as Joyful Responsible Abundance. [1, pp. 3-7; T10]

rows: Access to intelligence
Does this help with my task, language and access needs?
Task results, sources, support and available arrangements.
Learning and livelihoods
What could I learn, make, practise or offer?
Invitations, costs, access, paid/voluntary status and demonstrated skill or work.
Shared computing
Would shared capacity suit a job I do not want to buy equipment for?
Availability, operator access, performance, cost, governance and migration.
Ownership and enterprise
What share would people have in the productive capability?
Ownership terms, responsibilities, funding and distribution of benefits.
Freedom over time
Does this reduce burdens or create room for care, creativity or rest?
Observed time and effort; funded time away from work has its own arrangement.
Democratic participation
Which decisions affect my life, and how might I help shape them?
Sources, responsible bodies, genuine responses, amendments and outcomes.

blocks.text: Joyful Responsible Abundance
Joyful: more room for relationships, curiosity, creativity, belonging, rest and enjoyment.
Responsible: care for consequences, including who benefits, who carries costs, effects on other people and the environment, and what reaches future generations.

Abundance: wider access to useful knowledge, resources, care, opportunity and the ability to participate. The three ideas together ask whether growing capability makes life more worth living and its benefits more widely shared. [1, pp. 2-3]

title: Community contribution
description: Recognise voluntary contribution while the agent handles the records.

blocks.text: One Community-Hour, or C-Hour, recognises one verified hour of voluntary human contribution. [4, pp. 10-11]
C-Hours would recognise everyday care, informal help, mentoring and organised community activity. The record would preserve what the person contributed and learned, and who benefited.
Let the agent handle the records

An Aura would use conversation, agreed activity details and personally chosen sources to prepare contribution recognition. It would remember recurring arrangements and ask briefly when something is unclear. A host, peer or recipient could help confirm an account where their judgement adds value. The person could correct a record through the same conversation. [4, pp. 9-11, 39-40]
Community recognition and reciprocity

Communities would choose their own thanks, shared experiences and reciprocal opportunities. Contributions shorter than an hour would count proportionately. The recognition carries no monetary value or financial entitlement; the supporting software would keep money, paid work, human contribution and outcomes distinct. [4, pp. 10-14, 36-40]
Participants and organisers would help shape the interactions and test whether recognition saves effort, supports relationships and makes taking part more enjoyable.
A more accessible community gathering
In this fictional example, a resident notices that the route to a gathering is difficult for people using mobility aids and talks it through with their Aura.
Finding a way forward

Aura would help describe the problem, locate the responsible organisation and compare an immediate access arrangement with a longer-term improvement. The resident would share the useful photograph and question through P4A and follow the receiving organisation's response.
Taking part

A volunteer helps prepare the gathering for 80 minutes. Their Aura would draw on agreed activity information and a brief conversation to prepare recognition of 1 1/3 C-Hours, asking for clarification where needed. Another participant could help where their knowledge is useful. The community would choose its thanks. [4, pp. 9-12]
Seeing what changes

The organisers' tools would bring together the access request, supplies, paid coordination and voluntary contribution. Afterwards, people would describe whether access improved and follow any remaining work with the responsible organisation.
The personal Aura would retain the participant's relevant records. The shared project would show what changed, what helped and what people want to improve next.

title: Public participation through P4A
description: Understand issues, compare proposals and follow public decisions.

blocks.text: Purple Party for Australia (P4A) is a proposed political party and public interface for democratic participation. It would help people understand public issues, compare possible changes and connect discussion with sources, proposals, responsible organisations and decisions. [1, p. 6; 4, pp. 15-18]

rows: Issue and place
The account, the relevant place or asset, affected people and what remains unknown.
Evidence and alternatives
Dated sources, observations, interpretations, options, assumptions and uncertainty.
Process and responsibility
Who owns the asset or operates the process, its scope, participants and relevant dates.
Proposal and discussion
A proposal, expected benefits, costs/resources, objections and amendments.
Decision and response
Who decided, what was decided, reasons, reference and a review or correction route.
Delivery and outcome
What was done and what changed against the original situation, including burden or harm.

blocks.text: Follow the public process

The record would show whether an issue is under discussion, submitted to consultation, awaiting a response or decided. Submitted requests would retain the receiving organisation's acknowledgement, reference and next review date.
Resident and visitor participation

Residents could follow continuing local proposals; visitors could contribute observations and join community activities. Formal processes would display their eligibility rules. Topics could range from local assets and services to legal and constitutional proposals.

description: Explore shared capability, practical household tools and place-based science.

What learning, support or work invitation is available?

Which values, practical work and relationships matter in this place?

blocks.text: Everyday planning and wellbeing

Kitchen Mate could help plan meals around available food, personal preferences and daily routines. Garden Mate could support growing and harvesting; Fermentation Mate could help preserve surplus. Together, these tools could reduce avoidable food waste, save time and support wellbeing. [4, pp. 13-14]
Personal and place-based science

Sovereign Space Builder proposes models of places, resources and possible changes. The Web3 Sensorium proposes connecting observations, scientific models and debate across independently operated systems. Participants could contribute records and model results through agreed shared projects. [6-7]

title: Preparing the proposed trial
description: The local programme, equipment, funding and responsibilities to agree before a public invitation.

blocks.text: A trial on Minjerribah and across Redlands would require hosts, funding, tested equipment and agreed operating responsibilities. First Nations participation and cultural material would follow agreements with the appropriate people. [5, pp. 9-11]

rows: Local programme
Agree the hosts, venues, activities, staffing, contact arrangements and council or community processes involved.
Equipment and budget
Inventory reusable equipment; test computers with the intended sensors and applications; price missing components, transport, installation and support.
Station and software
Complete the flatpack design, stability and access checks; test assembly, capture, calibration, application performance and session handover.
Personal records
Demonstrate device or browser collection, permissions, export, correction, deletion and recovery, including treatment of public-station session data.
Community connections
Test conversational contribution recognition with participants and organisers, and connect civic submissions with the responsible receiving channels.
Access and assistance
Arrange suitable interfaces, language support, physical access and assisted participation for people without their own device.

blocks.text: Review the results

A review would examine completed tasks, measurement quality, application reliability, privacy, costs and support effort. Participant feedback would cover what helped, what failed and what prevented access. Civic cases would track submissions, responses, decisions and observed outcomes.
